legend: Vasya wrote down n$$$n$$$ consecutive positive integers on a piece of paper. In total, there are k$$$k$$$ digits written down. What number did Vasya write first?
input: Two integers n$$$n$$$ and k$$$k$$$ are given, each on a separate line (1≤n≤1017$$$1 \le n \le 10^{17}$$$, 1≤k≤min(18⋅n,1018)$$$1 \le k \le \min(18 \cdot n, 10^{18})$$$).
output: Output the number that was written first. If there are multiple correct answers, output the smallest one. If there are no solutions, output -1.
note: Subtask 1 (up to 28 points): n≤100$$$n \le 100$$$, k≤min(3⋅n,103)$$$k \le \min(3 \cdot n, 10^3)$$$.
Subtask 2 (up to 36 points): n≤106$$$n \le 10^6$$$, k≤min(7⋅n,107)$$$k \le \min(7 \cdot n, 10^7)$$$.

Note: The input data and answer in the third subtask may not fit into a 32-bit integer type, it is recommended to use a 64-bit type (long long in C++, long in Java and C#, int64 in Pascal). In Python, no additional actions are required.
